name: Tory
summary: Toryism is the British traditionalist strand of conservatism that grew out of the Cavalier royalists and the 17th-century party defending the Crown and the Church of England. It stands for monarchy, an established church, inherited institutions and a hierarchical but organic social order, and in its one-nation form holds that the governing classes owe responsibility to the poor and should reconcile the classes. It is cautious about reform, sceptical of abstract reason and doctrinaire markets or planning, and attached to nation and Empire.
scope: The British Tory tradition from the Stuart royalists through Burke, Disraeli's one-nation Toryism and the post-war paternalists, treated as traditionalist conservatism. It excludes the Canadian and American Tory usages and the free-market New Right. Many answers on modern issues are low-confidence inferences, since the sources document principles rather than programmes.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Later one-nation Conservatives accepted the post-war welfare state and the NHS.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: One-nation paternalism favours labour protection but nothing here addresses wage floors; adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Toryism is not doctrinaire about markets; they are accepted within custom, and Tories were split between protection and enterprise.

public-ownership.rationale: Post-war paternalists tolerated nationalised industry while others favoured enterprise; no settled Tory line.

property-fundamental.rationale: Burke tied liberties to landed property and conservatives value property as a support of social order.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Disraeli-era labour reforms show a willingness to regulate employers for the welfare of workers.

cut-welfare.rationale: Paternalism and the aim of reconciling the classes favour social provision over cutting it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The tradition did not address this; adherents split between order and liberty.

strong-leader.rationale: Tories defend the Crown, Parliament and inherited institutions rather than leaders bypassing them.

state-harmful.rationale: Toryism values authority and established institutions; the state is a necessary organ of the social order.

empower-police-military.rationale: Strong armed forces and order are described as hallmarks of later Toryism.

decide-locally.rationale: Local communities matter to the organic view, but Toryism also defends a central Crown and Parliament.

traditional-family.rationale: Family, property and religion are the institutions in which the conservative organic society places its faith.

more-religion-public.rationale: Tories historically stood for high-church Anglicanism and the established church: God, King and Country.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Tradition and patriotism are core conservative virtues, and the Tory motto names God, King and Country.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke's cautious, restorative reform is the model, and Tories opposed radical change.

free-trade.rationale: Documented split: most Tories backed Corn Law protection while Peelites embraced free trade.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Scepticism about progress and the limits of reason point away from technological optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Burke and the Tories opposed the French Revolution and favoured only cautious reform.

central-planning.rationale: Conservatives reject doctrinaire planning as well as doctrinaire laissez-faire.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tories were protectionist over agriculture in the Corn Law era but later accepted free trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Interventionism is a later Tory hallmark, but no stated view on strategic investment.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wholly opposed to the order Toryism defends.

one-party-rule.rationale: Toryism evolved in a parliamentary party system under the Crown.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Tories are monarchists; God, King or Queen and Country is the tradition's motto.

direct-votes.rationale: Burke questioned the head-count majority; representation by the qualified is preferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Tory loyalists opposed secession from the Crown and the Empire.

natural-rulers.rationale: High Tories defend hierarchy, natural order and aristocracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Royalist tradition fought civil wars but later Toryism stressed order; adherents split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Tories historically supported the established Church of England.

class-struggle-history.rationale: One-nation Toryism holds that classes should be reconciled, not set against each other.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Burke's order rests on inequality and hierarchy.

civilizational-union.rationale: Empire-Commonwealth ties mattered but no civilizational union is documented.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Noblesse oblige holds that the privileged owe duties, not mere self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Burke treats rights as inherited patrimony and society as a partnership across generations.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Coleridge and others criticised unchecked industrialisation but not civilisation as a whole.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Contrary to scepticism of abstract reason and faith in human institutions.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Conservatives are particularist sceptics of abstract principle and doctrine.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to the order Toryism defends.

collective-farming.rationale: Contrary to the defence of landed property.

taxation-theft.rationale: Conservatives treat the state as a necessary authority.

harm-principle.rationale: Paternalism holds the state should promote subjects' religion and morality, not only prevent harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Burke rejected abstract natural rights in favour of inherited rights within society.

total-state.rationale: Conservatism rejects doctrinaire planning and places faith in family, property and religion.

bound-labor.rationale: Disraeli condemned the serfage of the poor.

single-common-good.rationale: One-nation ideal holds the elite should reconcile the interests of all classes.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Conservatives are sceptics about reason's pretensions and Tories valued church and tradition.

class-collaboration.rationale: One-nation Toryism wants the elite to reconcile labour and management interests.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Contrary to tradition as accumulated wisdom.

workers-nation.rationale: One-nation ideal rests on national rather than international class identity.

ban-interest.rationale: Contrary to acceptance of property and commerce.

state-class-instrument.rationale: One-nation Toryism holds that government reconciles all classes.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial claim contrary to establishment Toryism.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Paternalist state promotes subjects' welfare beyond defence and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Christian moral equality coexists with hierarchy of station; split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Stuart legitimism rejected contractual consent while later Toryism accepted parliamentary government.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionist era leaned this way, later Tories did not.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Class cooperation and paternalism cut against struggle as the engine.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Disraeli held that those in power owe obligations to the condition of the people.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Later Conservative policy but not a Tory principle.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: One-nation figures and the New Right split.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces owe loyalty to the Crown.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Toryism is attached to nation, Crown and parliamentary sovereignty, and modern Tories lean Eurosceptic, though some one-nation Conservatives backed European union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: High Tories defend the Crown's prerogative to command the forces and appoint ministers, but the settled British Tory view accepts ministers answerable to Parliament, so support is a qualified lean.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Tory party arose to defend the Church of England and its episcopal order against dissent and congregational Puritanism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Tories defend an established church alongside the Crown and Parliament, not rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Toryism is bound to nation, Crown and Empire, and treats wartime disloyalty as treason.

recall-officials.rationale: Burke's Tory view is that representatives exercise independent judgment and are judged at elections, which is incompatible with recall.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burkean Toryism opposes remaking a constitution from scratch by assembly, preferring inherited institutions and gradual reform.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Toryism is monarchist and defends an inherited head of state against election.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Burkean and one-nation Toryism treat property as carrying duties to those beneath, with the governing classes owing responsibility to the poor.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Toryism defended an empire acquired partly by conquest but also prized law and prescription; adherents are split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale turns on church property, privileges or separation, and the statement now asks only whether religious institutions should operate under the government's authority.

reviewHistory.rationale: Tories defend the established Church of England and its endowments against civil encroachment.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale turns on church property, privileges or separation, and the statement now asks only whether religious institutions should operate under the government's authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Tories defend the Crown as a symbol of national continuity standing above party.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Tories prize ancient law and the constitution, and Burke held rulers bound by the laws and customs of the realm.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The mixed British constitution of Crown, Lords and Commons is the classic Tory ideal.

equal-parenting.rationale: Toryism does not address custody law; adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: One-nation Toryism seeks cooperation between classes, so a doctrine of continuing class struggle is alien to it.

land-redistribution.rationale: Tories defend inherited property and the landed order; breaking up estates is the opposite of this.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Conservative thought stresses tradition, authority and custom over economic determinism as shaping society.

ban-cartels.rationale: Paternalists accept some regulation of economic power, but Toryism has no settled view on antitrust; adherents split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Corn Law protectionism and imperial preference are in the tradition, but a full shut-off bloc is not; adherents split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Burkean conservatism rejects revolution and abstract schemes, preferring gradual change within tradition.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Monarchy, aristocracy and hierarchy are core to the tradition.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Attachment to Empire is documented, and Tories later favoured the Commonwealth and continuing ties.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: One-nation Toryism stresses class cooperation and the shared national interest over class conflict.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Burkean conservatism trusts inherited constitution and parliamentary sovereignty over written, entrenched rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: Toryism defends hereditary monarchy and inherited institutions.

minority-veto.rationale: An organic, hierarchical order with authority and tradition rules out individual consent as the basis of binding decisions.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Noblesse oblige is the defining ethic of one-nation Toryism, and Disraeli's Sybil urges it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Respect for tradition and inherited institutions favours keeping them.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Burkean conservatism holds that institutions grow organically from each people's history.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Burke and the tradition tie liberty to inherited landed property, so common land tenure is opposed.

job-guarantee.rationale: One-nation paternalism supports welfare but not a formal job guarantee; adherents split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Burkean and Tory thought treats authority and inherited law as binding in themselves.

industrial-unions.rationale: One-nation Toryism favoured class cooperation but did not address union structure; adherents split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Toryism defends the established church and inherited institutions, marriage among them.

informal-organisation.rationale: Conservatism prizes established, hierarchical institutions over ad hoc groups.

religious-nation.rationale: Toryism defends the established Church of England as part of national identity, though modern Tories accept pluralism.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Tory conservatism defends property and hierarchy and opposes common ownership of the means of production.

religion-illusion.rationale: Toryism defends an established church and holds religion to meet lasting human needs.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Disraeli's Sybil criticises industrial inequality while Tories accepted commerce; adherents are split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Hierarchy, private property and inherited institutions are opposed to communal reorganisation of society.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Burkean Toryism defends constitutional order and the loyal opposition; suppressing opposition is arbitrary power, not ordered liberty.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Tories were attached to Empire and protection, but Burkean trusteeship also stressed duty to subject peoples; adherents split.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Burke's conservatism holds that legitimacy comes from prescription and settled constitution, and treats forcible removal of rulers as revolutionary.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Burkean representation holds that elected representatives judge for the nation rather than act as delegates of direct popular decision.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation is a Marxian concept; Disraeli's Sybil criticises the condition of workers but blames lost aristocratic duty, not capitalism as such.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Toryism grew out of royalism defending the Crown by divine right, and Burke saw the state as divinely ordained, though modern Tories hold this loosely.

social-market-economy.rationale: One-nation Toryism accepted markets within social responsibility, the post-war welfare state and class reconciliation, against both laissez-faire and planning.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Toryism stands for Crown, nation and Empire, and so for strong armed forces.

rich-first.rationale: Hierarchy is accepted but noblesse oblige requires the better-off to look after the poor, and Tories split on trickle-down.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a constitutional or ceremonial crown, and the statement now asks only about passing real governing power to a child.

reviewHistory.rationale: Toryism is defined by loyalty to the Crown and hereditary monarchy, which passes from parent to child.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale is about a constitutional or ceremonial crown, and the statement now asks only about passing real governing power to a child.

property-franchise.rationale: Traditional Toryism accepted a franchise tied to property and a stake in the land, though one-nation Tories later backed extensions such as Disraeli's 1867 Act.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Tories defend the rule of law and the ancient constitution, and Burkean conservatism values settled law over arbitrary decree.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Toryism defends the established Church of England and the Crown, so an atheist state education programme is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Conservatism prizes order, authority and inherited institutions, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: One-nation Toryism combines paternalist duty and voluntary community with acceptance of state welfare, so adherents split on which does better.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Tories defend property while paternalists want responsibility toward the poor; split.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Burkean Tories see the nation as an inherited, organic continuity across generations.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Toryism does not address the role of a homeland for a diaspora; adherents are split.

online-anonymity.rationale: Toryism never addressed online anonymity; authority favours accountability but tradition also values privacy, so adherents split.

person-over-state.rationale: Toryism sees the person as embedded in an organic society with duties, yet paternalism protects the individual's welfare; adherents are split.

dense-cities.rationale: Toryism is silent on urban form; its rural, landed heritage and its support for cities pull in different directions.

racial-pride.rationale: Toryism prizes national and imperial pride but does not address racial pride as such; adherents split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Burke's conservatism opposes violent overthrow of inherited institutions and favours cautious reform (s3).

nature-as-capital.rationale: Toryism stresses stewardship but does not address pricing nature; adherents split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Burke's organic society is a partnership between the dead, the living and the unborn, which gives individual lives meaning through the nation (s3).

student-debt-relief.rationale: Toryism does not address student loans; adherents are split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Toryism values the countryside and stewardship but also property and liberty; the sources do not settle it.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Toryism defends an established Church of England, which gives one tradition a privileged legal position.

national-church-status.rationale: Toryism is defined by defence of the established Church of England as the national church with a special place in law.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Toryism defends intermediate institutions, parliament and the party system as parts of the organic order, against leaders appealing past them.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Toryism defends an established Church of England woven into the constitution, so religion in public life is accepted.

multipolar-world.rationale: Tories prized the balance of power in Europe, but also Empire and national preeminence; the sources do not take a stance on this question.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Tory conservatism is sceptical of abstract theory and doctrinaire planning, and as the Stanford entry describes it, rests on tradition rather than Marxist economics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: One-nation Toryism joins attachment to nation with responsibility for the poor, as in Disraeli's Sybil and the two-nations idea.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Toryism is a monarchist, church-and-crown tradition opposed to communist rule, and so does not endorse socialism under party leadership.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Paternalism and the aim of reconciling the classes favour social provision over cutting it. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Those with wealth and rank owe obligations to the poor beneath them.
missingStatements.rationale: Noblesse oblige is the defining ethic of one-nation Toryism, and Disraeli's Sybil is written to expose neglect of the people.

missingStatements.text: A hereditary aristocracy should keep a role in governing the country.
missingStatements.rationale: High Tories defend hierarchy, natural order and aristocracy.

notes: High Tories and one-nation paternalists would diverge from the free-market Thatcherite wing, which is excluded here; modern Conservative Party members vary widely on social issues.
